definitions.gloss: to exert an influence; to have an effect on; to impact
definitions.explanation: To produce a noticeable effect or influence on something or someone. Used for both positive and negative impacts. A formal expression common in news, academic writing, and official reports.

examples.japanese: {健康|けんこう}に{影響|えいきょう}を{及|およ}ぼす。
{環境|かんきょう}に{悪|わる}い{影響|えいきょう}を{及|およ}ぼす{恐|おそ}れがある。
examples.english: There is a risk of having a negative effect on the environment.

examples.japanese: この{政策|せいさく}は{経済|けいざい}{全体|ぜんたい}に{大|おお}きな{影響|えいきょう}を{及|およ}ぼすと{予想|よそう}されている。
examples.english: This policy is expected to have a major impact on the economy as a whole.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal expression frequently used in written Japanese, news, and academic contexts. The verb {及|およ}ぼす specifically means to extend or reach, giving the expression a sense of influence spreading outward. Often modified with {良|よ}い/{悪|わる}い (good/bad) or {大|おお}きな (large) to specify the nature of the impact.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {悪|わる}い{影響|えいきょう}を{及|およ}ぼす (to have a bad effect)
- {良|よ}い{影響|えいきょう}を{及|およ}ぼす (to have a good effect)
- {大|おお}きな{影響|えいきょう}を{及|およ}ぼす (to have a major impact)
- {深刻|しんこく}な{影響|えいきょう}を{及|およ}ぼす (to have a serious impact)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}える: to give influence — a slightly less formal synonym
- {影響|えいきょう}する: to influence — the simplest way to express this
